source.title: Overparameterized ReLU Neural Networks Learn the Simplest Model: Neural Isometry and Phase Transitions
source.authors: Yifei Wang; Yixuan Hua; Emmanuel J. Candes; Mert Pilanci

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices. Some equations and figure content are flattened, but relevant stated text and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks recover planted simple models and how sample-to-dimension ratio and architecture affect generalization, using recovery and test-error measures rather than the claim versions’ natural-label classification settings.
record.gate_note: Results on planted linear and ReLU labels, noisy observations, and empirical test error bear on V2’s width/generalization relationship and on conditions affecting a training–test gap. Cited studies and background claims about optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, and memorization are not this paper’s own results.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes planted-model recovery as sample count and input dimension vary, using minimum-norm interpolation or explicit weight decay. It does not test V2's decrease in test error when width increases beyond interpolation. Nor does it test any other listed version; CNN comparisons are prior work or future directions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish data conditions under which global minimum-norm or weight-decay-regularized solutions recover simple planted models despite arbitrarily many neurons, with sample-dependent recovery transitions and extensions to bounded noise. They leave the behavior of non-convex training, which may reach local minima, open.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic Gaussian, Haar, and sub-Gaussian inputs with planted linear or ReLU labels, two-layer ReLU networks, and weight decay or minimum-norm interpolation. It does not reproduce natural-label memorization/generalization experiments or a width sweep of test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Sample-to-dimension ratio (notably n/d around 2); skip connections and normalization layers; planted-model and data assumptions; noise level and regularization parameter β; convex versus non-convex training.

fits_no_version.finding: Minimum-norm ReLU networks with skip connections recover planted linear models above a sample-to-dimension threshold. Below it, non-uniqueness depends on the planted parameter's activation condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified Gaussian-data and optimality assumptions, planted linear recovery depends on sample geometry and can hold with arbitrarily many neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-epoch AdamW experiments report test-error transitions around n = 2d for skip-connected and normalized networks, with width tied to sample count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization in these synthetic planted-model experiments varies with sample-to-dimension ratio and training procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: With sufficiently many sub-Gaussian samples, bounded noise, and a suitable weight-decay interval, optimal networks select only a linear component with a bounded estimation error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit regularization can select simple linear models from overparameterized ReLU networks despite observation noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Neural Isometry Conditions guarantee recovery of planted ReLU neurons; theoretical and numerical results also address multiple planted neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under appropriate data conditions, global minimum-norm solutions recover sparse planted ReLU models despite excess network capacity.

record.problems: The theoretical results require synthetic planted-model assumptions and specified data regularity conditions, so they do not directly test natural-label classification. Empirical experiments generally use 5 trials for convex recovery plots and 10 for non-convex test-error plots. The non-convex experiments may reach local minima. Several relevant test-error values are only shown in figures, without numeric reporting in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. V3 receives tested_not_extracted because the paper discusses CNN convex formulations as prior work and states that CNN and transformer architectures are future directions; it does not report its own CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison. V1 and V4–V8 are not tested; related discussion in the introduction cites prior work only.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether increasing width beyond zero training error keeps lowering test error in networks trained to convergence without explicit regularization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, and recovery through optimizer changes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Delete both V2 limits_scope verdicts: failure to test the width trend is an untested part, not evidence limiting it. Change V3 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. The paper's sample thresholds should not be interpreted as width interpolation thresholds.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization on CIFAR-10 or ImageNet.
A width sweep past the interpolation threshold on natural labels; the paper uses networks with arbitrary neuron counts in theory, but does not report test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the local-connectivity mechanism.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ReLU network with skip connection, convex program (11)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical recovery result as sample count n crosses 2d for Gaussian data and planted linear labels.

conditions.value: noiseless planted linear model y = Xw*

rows.measure: Unique recovery of planted linear model (implies perfect generalization under the planted model).
rows.baseline: Recovery fails with high probability when n < 2d, under the stated Xw* ≥ 0 condition.
rows.value: For n > 2d, unique recovery with probability at least 1 − exp(−αn), α = (n/2−d)^2/(64n^2).
rows.uncertainty: High-probability bound as stated; numerical experiment uses 5 independent trials.
rows.note: The result concerns recovery of a planted linear function on Gaussian inputs, not a natural-label task. Theory says arbitrary neuron count; the empirical recovery plots use a convex group-Lasso formulation.
rows.check: Theorem 5 establishes planted linear recovery above n = 2d, not a width-dependent decrease in test error. Its stated probability bound is correctly extracted. The below-threshold baseline requires Xw* ≥ 0; Proposition 7 reports unique recovery when that condition fails and d < n < 2d.

rows.subject: ReLU network with skip connection, convex program (11)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical recovery result below the sample threshold for Gaussian data.

conditions.value: planted linear model y = Xw*, with Xw* ≥ 0

rows.measure: Whether the planted linear model is the unique optimal solution.
rows.baseline: Unique recovery is guaranteed above n > 2d.
rows.value: With probability 1, the planted linear model is not the unique optimal solution.
rows.uncertainty: Theorem states probability 1; the surrounding argument describes the all-ones pattern event as high probability.
rows.note: The theorem is restricted to planted parameters satisfying Xw* ≥ 0; this is not a test-error measurement.
rows.check: Non-uniqueness of minimum-norm recovery under Xw* ≥ 0 is not partial evidence for V2. The row reports no comparison of test errors across widths. Preserve the theorem's conditional probability-one statement rather than generalizing failure to all planted parameters.

rows.subject: ReLU network with skip connection, regularized non-convex training problem (6)
rows.operation_detail: Non-convex training with AdamW and weight decay β = 10⁻⁶; empirical test error measured against a planted linear model.

conditions.value: planted linear model, noiseless and noisy conditions

rows.measure: Test error; the paper describes a transition around n = 2d and says test error increases as n/d increases.
rows.value: Figure 8: figure only; text states test error increases as n/d increases and the rate of increase becomes sharper around n = 2d.
rows.uncertainty: 10 independent trials; no numerical uncertainty stated.
rows.note: The prose describes the trend, but numerical test-error values and a direction relative to a baseline are not supplied. The authors also caution that non-convex training may reach local minimizers.
rows.check: The experiment varies n and d with m = n + 1, confounding width with sample count. It uses weight decay and 400 epochs, without establishing convergence or a width threshold for interpolation. The reported increasing-error direction matches the prose, but numerical values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ReLU network with normalization layer, regularized non-convex training problem (6)
rows.operation_detail: Non-convex training with AdamW and weight decay β = 10⁻⁶; empirical test error measured against a planted normalized ReLU neuron.

conditions.value: planted normalized ReLU neuron, noiseless and noisy conditions

rows.measure: Test error; text says it increases as n/d increases and its rate of increase becomes sharp around n = 2d.
rows.value: Figure 25: figure only; trend described in text.
rows.uncertainty: 10 independent trials; no numerical uncertainty stated.
rows.note: The figure’s plotted values are not reported numerically in the supplied text; non-convex training may reach local minimizers.
rows.check: The normalized-network experiment varies sample count and dimension with m = n + 1, rather than isolating width beyond interpolation. It uses explicit weight decay and finite training. The increasing-error description matches the prose; the supplied figure text provides no numerical values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Theoretical minimum-norm recovery for planted linear labels on Gaussian data
reader_labels.reason: Recovery changes sharply with sample ratio: unique recovery is given for n > 2d, while non-uniqueness occurs for n < 2d under Xw* ≥ 0 (R1–R2); these results do not establish that widening beyond interpolation lowers test error.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Non-convex empirical training on planted labels
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports a test-error transition around n = 2d, but gives figure-only values and notes local-minimum risk, so the claimed width trend is not established (R3–R4).
